Mice were assessed on their capacity to learn the location of an escape box over four days of training and the latency to locate the box was taken as a measure of spatial learning. Curiously, Y exercise mice showed longer latencies to the escape box compared to control mice on training days 1, 3 and 4 (p = 0.017, p = 0.011 and p < 0.001) (Figure 8A) however this was largely explained by increased latencies for female mice to locate the escape box on days 2, 3, and 4 (p = 0.026, p = 0.006, and p = 0.0003). There were no differences in training day latencies evident in M mice, but exercise mice displayed increased latencies on day 2 in O mice (p < 0.001)(Figure 8B-C).

(D) Long-term memory of context fear conditioning. CCX increased the time spent in the center of the ﬁeld, which is usually taken as a fear-related index [7]. Previous studies showed that CCX increased the basal testosterone secretion of the right testis and the serum follicle-stimulating hormone con- centration in adult left hemiorchidectomized rats [2]. Such an involvement of CC in an asymmetrical pituitary-independent control of testicular steroidogenesis might be a candidate mech- anism for the alteration of fear-related behaviors associated with CCX. The alteration of opiate pathways following CCX might also contribute to these behavioral modiﬁcations [9]. In the present study, housing had signiﬁcant effects on the fre- quency of rearing and teeth-chattering, that is, EE increased the frequency of rearing and IE reduced the frequency of teeth- chattering.
